GENERAL REQUIREMENTS AND ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA FOR FORKLIFT TRUCKS WITH CAPACITY FROM 10 000 kg TO 50000 kg
1. Scope-Covers the general requirements and tests for verification with capacity varying from 10000 kg to 50 000 kg. 2. Terminology 2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the terms and definitions terms relating to fork arms and attachments of forklift trucks, 2.2 The rated capacity of a forklift truck is the load, permitted type is capable of transporting or lifting in normal operation given in IS : 7570-I 975 `Glossary of along with the following shall apply by the manufacturer, that the truck under specific conditions. of stability of forklift trucks

2.3 The actual capacity of a forklift truck is the maximum load in kg (depending upon its elevating height and/or attachment), permitted by the manufacturer (usually by stability testing), that thr subject truck is capable of transportrng or lifting in normal operation under specific conditions 3. 3.2.1 The actual capacity of a truck is-derived from the appropriate stability tests and shall vary with different types and heights of mast fittedand different load centre distances (see 3.1.3 ) used in the rating. The rating shall be determined with fork arms or platform provided by the manufacturer. Additional actual capacity ratings with removable attachments may also be established where permitted by the appropriate stability specification. 3.2.2 The forklift trucks (travelling with the load at normal travelling height and stacking) freight containers shall have satisfactory stability when reasonably and appropriately conditions where the wind speed is up to 45 km/h (Beaufort Scale Force 6). 3.3 Lifting and Tilting Mechanism handling used in

3.3.1 Chains-Only leaf and roller mechanism chains shall be used. When the lifting mechanism includes a chain or chains, the truck manufacturer shall select chain, which in relation to the minimum breaking load certified by the manufacturer of the chain, shall provide a factor, K (as given by the following formula) in relation to the static load that would exist in a single chain or in equally loaded chains when the maximum rated load is in the transporting position, assuming no friction in the mast structure: K = 5 where C = truck rated capacity in tonnes, load per and or wire + rope Dead the x weight pitch Number of lift chains devrce or wire ropes 0.2 (C10)

986 EXPLANATORY NOTE

Heavy capacity forklift trucks are generally used for handling freight containers and this standard is prepared keeping in view the heavy traffic of containers in our country. Standardization of such forklift trucks would ensure safe and correct interchangeability of heavy materials. In the preparation of this standard, the considerable assistance has bee,, derived from FEM Section IV-Industrial trucks `Safety code for powered industrial trucks', issued by Federation Europelnne de la Manutention (FEM).
